For \(i=1\), \(a_1+b_1=c_1\), so \((1,1)\) lies on \(l_1\).
For \(i=2\), \(a_2+b_2=2c_2\), so \(\left(\frac12,\frac12\right)\) lies on \(l_2\).

Let \(A=(1,1)\), \(B=\left(\frac12,\frac12\right)\). Then
\[
|AB|=\sqrt{\left(\frac12\right)^2+\left(\frac12\right)^2}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}.
\]
The condition forces \(l_1\parallel l_2\), and the distance between them is exactly \(|AB|\), so both lines are perpendicular to \(AB\). Hence their normal vectors are parallel to \((1,1)\), giving
\[
a_1=b_1,\qquad a_2=b_2.
\]
Thus
\[
c_1=a_1+b_1=2a_1 \implies \frac{c_1}{a_1}=2,
\]
and
\[
a_2+b_2=2c_2 \implies 2a_2=2c_2 \implies \frac{a_2}{c_2}=1.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\frac{c_1}{a_1}+\frac{a_2}{c_2}=2+1=3.
\]

\[
\boxed{3}
\]
